claim: Choose an execution route per business operation, accounting for coverage, authorization, verification and recovery.
counter_evidence: A single route can be sufficient for a small complete workflow.
uncertainty: This is a design inference, not a measured ranking.

claim: Stripe API v1 response replay and key retention do not give unlimited retry protection.
uncertainty: Other providers and endpoints have their own contracts.

claim: Stripe API v2 has a 30-day replay scope and can retry failed work while preserving successful work.
counter_evidence: Some requests cannot be successfully replayed.
uncertainty: Applies only within documented same-key/API/account-or-sandbox conditions.

claim: An actionability-checked browser click does not by itself verify the application business state.
counter_evidence: Some low-consequence read-only tasks can be checked entirely through displayed content.
uncertainty: The required outcome evidence depends on the application.

claim: DOM automation and visual model control have different interaction and maintenance surfaces.
counter_evidence: A model may generate DOM actions; real systems can combine methods.
uncertainty: The categories describe mechanisms, not mutually exclusive products.

claim: An API does not remove injection risk when the model interprets untrusted text returned by that API.
counter_evidence: Deterministic consumers that do not interpret text as instructions have a different threat model.
uncertainty: No comparative incident rate is available in the reviewed sources.

claim: Browser session isolation and application authorization address different boundaries.
counter_evidence: An application may provide a dedicated restricted browser account.
uncertainty: No universal browser-versus-API permission ranking follows.

claim: A hybrid workflow needs recorded identities and a recovery boundary before another external write.
counter_evidence: A fully covered API-only or DOM-only workflow can avoid this extra boundary. New API coverage alone does not establish that migrating an existing hybrid is worth its cost.
uncertainty: The support-ticket walkthrough is illustrative and untested.

claim: Cost comparisons should include verification, failed attempts, maintenance and human exceptions over a common workload.
counter_evidence: A low-volume browser workflow can avoid disproportionate integration work.
uncertainty: No throughput, price or completion-rate measurements were collected.

claim: HTTP 202 reports acceptance rather than completed processing.
uncertainty: The meaning of other success codes and the business outcome depends on the endpoint.
